Release it if you want, genius. I'll slap a part in and you'll pay through the nose.

lines: Go ahead and release it, your call. But the shop fills that slot at a markup, and fetching the part yourself comes out cheaper.
Every patched panel and tool on this wall is mine, and I squeeze every last bit out of a part. Even a rushed shop part costs extra.
Release it if you like, it's your ship. I'll fit a stock part in the empty slot, but it'll cost you more than doing it yourself.

report.reason: Line 2 is proud and grinning. Lines 1 and 3 are friendly and cheeky enough, with a light grin and no meanness. They are mild, and nothing in them is unkind to the player.
Nothing sounds rich, high-tech or wasteful. Line 2 leans into squeezing every bit out of a part, and the others are neutral.
Only the mechanic speaks. No other mechanics, crew, boss or successor is mentioned.

Lines 1 and 3 make clear the shop fills the slot at a premium, that doing it yourself is cheaper, and that releasing is the player's call. Line 2 never says the player could buy the part cheaper themselves and never leaves the release to the player, so it misses the moment's job. As a set, one of three lines misses.
